intent.raw_query: Greece under $2000, beaches and local food, summer, flying from NYC

experiences.name: Navagio Beach (Shipwreck Beach) Visit
experiences.description: Take a boat tour to the iconic Navagio Beach on Zakynthos, one of Greece's most photographed beaches. The stunning turquoise waters, towering limestone cliffs, and the famous shipwreck make this an unmissable experience. Boat tours depart regularly from Porto Vromi or Zakynthos Town.

experiences.name: Athens Central Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the vibrant Varvakios Agora (Athens Central Market) and surrounding streets packed with local vendors selling fresh seafood, olives, cheeses, spices, and cured meats. Sample street food like souvlaki, spanakopita, and loukoumades from nearby stalls. A guided walking food tour enhances the experience with cultural context.

experiences.name: Elafonissi Beach Day Trip
experiences.description: Visit the breathtaking Elafonissi Beach in southwestern Crete, famous for its pink-tinged sand and shallow crystal-clear lagoon. Wade across the sandbar to the small island, snorkel in the warm Aegean waters, and relax in one of Greece's most naturally beautiful beach settings. Accessible by bus or rental car from Chania.

experiences.name: Traditional Cretan Cooking Class
experiences.description: Join a hands-on cooking class in Chania focused on authentic Cretan cuisine, one of the healthiest diets in the world. Learn to prepare dishes like dakos (barley rusk salad), lamb with stamnagathi greens, and honey-drizzled kalitsounia pastries using locally sourced ingredients. Classes typically include a market visit and a full meal.

experiences.name: Mykonos Beach Club & Local Taverna Evening
experiences.description: Spend the afternoon at Paradise Beach or Psarou Beach on Mykonos, enjoying the golden sand and clear blue waters. As the sun sets, head to a local taverna in Mykonos Town (Chora) for a traditional Greek dinner featuring fresh grilled octopus, tzatziki, fresh-caught fish, and local Assyrtiko wine at a fraction of the beach club prices.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Greece
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 14:50
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Athens International Airport (Eleftherios Venizelos) at 14:50. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take the budget-friendly X95 express bus (€6) to central Athens. Check into your hostel or budget guesthouse in the Monastiraki or Psiri neighborhood. Freshen up and get oriented.
day_by_day.evening: Take a relaxed evening stroll through Monastiraki Square and the Plaka neighborhood. Explore the atmospheric old streets, browse local shops, and soak in your first Greek evening atmosphere. Watch the sunset over the Acropolis from a free street-level viewpoint.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a snack at the airport
meals.lunch: Grab a quick gyros pita wrap from a street kiosk near Monastiraki (€2.50–€3.50)
meals.dinner: Eat at a traditional taverna in Psiri neighborhood — try moussaka or souvlaki plate with bread and a local beer (€8–€12 total)

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 activities begin only after 14:50 arrival. Book budget accommodation in Monastiraki or Psiri in advance — hostels average €15–€25/night. Keep cash on hand for buses and street food.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Acropolis early (opens 8:00 AM) to beat the heat and crowds. Climb up to see the Parthenon, Erechtheion, and Propylaea. Purchase a combined ticket (€30) that covers multiple Athens archaeological sites valid for 5 days — excellent value.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk downhill to explore the Ancient Agora (included in combined ticket), the ancient marketplace of Athens. Afterward, wander through the Monastiraki Flea Market browsing vintage goods, local crafts, and souvenirs at negotiable prices.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Thissio neighborhood for a scenic evening walk along the Apostolou Pavlou pedestrian promenade with Acropolis views. Find a quiet spot to sit and enjoy the golden hour light on the ancient ruins.

meals.breakfast: Grab a tiropita (cheese pie) and Greek coffee from a local bakery near your hostel (€2–€3)
meals.lunch: Souvlaki wrap from a street stall near Monastiraki — one of Athens' best budget meals (€2.50–€3)
meals.dinner: Traditional taverna in Thissio — try grilled octopus, Greek salad, and house wine (€10–€14)

day_by_day.notes: Go to the Acropolis as early as possible — by 10 AM it gets very crowded and hot. Wear comfortable shoes and bring water. The combined archaeological ticket saves significant money if you plan to visit multiple sites.

day_by_day.morning: Use your combined ticket to visit the National Archaeological Museum (separate ticket €12 but worth it, or prioritize if budget is tight). Alternatively, visit the Acropolis Museum (€10) which houses stunning original sculptures and artifacts from the Acropolis hill.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the colorful Exarchia neighborhood — Athens' bohemian district with street art, independent bookshops, and a vibrant local atmosphere. Visit the nearby Strefi Hill park for a free panoramic view of Athens without the tourist crowds.
day_by_day.evening: Experience the Athens Central Market (Varvakios Agora) area in the early evening — a lively and authentic Greek experience. Walk through Omonia Square and surrounding streets to observe everyday Athenian life.

meals.breakfast: Koulouri (sesame bread ring) bought from a street cart — classic Athenian breakfast (€0.50–€1)
meals.lunch: Eat at a local laiki (street market) food stall in Exarchia for fresh, cheap mezedes and bread (€4–€6)
meals.dinner: Psarotaverna (fish taverna) near Omonia — grilled fresh fish with salad and tzatziki (€10–€15)

day_by_day.notes: Exarchia is perfectly safe for tourists during the day and evening. The neighborhood gives you an authentic non-touristy Athens experience. June weather averages 23°C — light layers for evening are recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Take the early metro (Line 1) from Athens to Piraeus port. Board a budget ferry to the island of Aegina — only 35–40 minutes away and one of the cheapest island day trips from Athens (ferry ~€9 each way). Arrive and rent a bicycle (€5–€8/day) to explore.
day_by_day.afternoon: Cycle or take a local bus to the stunning Temple of Aphaia — one of Greece's best-preserved ancient temples with beautiful hillside views. Afterward, head to the fishing village of Perdika on the southern tip for a swim at its clear turquoise beach.
day_by_day.evening: Return by ferry to Piraeus and head back to Athens by metro. Spend the evening relaxing in your neighborhood.

meals.breakfast: Eat before departure — grab pastry and coffee near your hostel (€2–€3)
meals.lunch: Fresh grilled fish and seafood at a harbourside taverna in Perdika village, Aegina (€10–€14)
meals.dinner: Budget souvlaki or gyros wrap back in Athens near Monastiraki (€3–€5)

day_by_day.notes: Check ferry schedules in advance at the Piraeus port or online. First ferry to Aegina typically departs around 7:00–8:00 AM. Aegina is also famous for pistachios — buy a bag as a cheap local snack (€3–€5).

day_by_day.morning: Pack your bags and take an early morning KTEL bus or ferry from Athens/Piraeus to the Peloponnese coast. Head to the charming coastal town of Nafplio — a 2.5-hour bus ride (~€13). Check into a budget guesthouse and drop your bags.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Nafplio's beautiful old town — one of Greece's most romantic and walkable cities. Visit the free waterfront promenade, browse the colorful neoclassical streets, and climb up to the Acronauplia fortress for free panoramic sea views.
day_by_day.evening: Walk along the waterfront esplanade at sunset. Watch local fishermen returning with their catch. Enjoy the relaxed Peloponnesian pace of life.

meals.breakfast: Quick bite before departure from Athens hostel or bus station café (€2–€4)
meals.lunch: Grab a gyros or pita wrap from a local fast-food spot in Nafplio after arriving (€2.50–€4)
meals.dinner: Traditional taverna in Nafplio old town — try the local specialty 'stifado' (meat stew) with local wine (€9–€13)

day_by_day.notes: KTEL buses from Athens to Nafplio depart from Kifissos Bus Terminal. Book a day ahead if possible. Nafplio budget guesthouses average €20–€35/night. The town is very walkable — no transport needed once you arrive.

day_by_day.morning: Take a local bus or taxi (shared cost if with others) to the ancient theater of Epidaurus — one of the most acoustically perfect and visually spectacular ancient sites in all of Greece. Admission is €12 (or included if you have a combined ticket). Explore at your own pace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Nafplio and spend the afternoon at Arvanitia Beach — a small, beautiful free public beach just a 10-minute walk from the old town. Swim in the clear Aegean waters and relax on the rocky shore.
day_by_day.evening: Climb the 999 steps to the iconic Palamidi Fortress (€8 entry) at sunset for breathtaking panoramic views over Nafplio, the bay, and surrounding mountains. The golden hour light here is spectacular.

meals.breakfast: Greek yogurt with local honey and walnuts from a bakery near your guesthouse (€3–€4)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or snacks from a local supermarket to eat at Epidaurus (€3–€5)
meals.dinner: Seaside taverna near the Nafplio waterfront — fresh grilled sea bream with Greek salad and local retsina wine (€11–€15)

day_by_day.notes: The bus to Epidaurus runs a few times daily — confirm the return schedule before you go. Palamidi Fortress is best visited in the late afternoon to avoid midday heat. Bring plenty of water for the climb.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning KTEL bus from Nafplio toward the Mani peninsula or continue to Kalamata (2–3 hours, ~€10–€15). Check into a budget room in Kalamata — the capital of the Peloponnese and famous for its olives. Explore the morning street market if it's running.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Kalamata's long sandy beach — one of the finest urban beaches in Greece, stretching 5+ kilometers with free access. Swim, sunbathe, and enjoy the warm June sea temperature (around 22–23°C). Rent a beach umbrella and chair for €5–€7.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through Kalamata's lively waterfront promenade lined with cafés and tavernas. Visit the historic kastro (castle) above the old town for free sunset views over the city and sea.

meals.breakfast: Fresh bread, local Kalamata olives, and feta from a market stall (€3–€4)
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood mezedes (small plates) at a beach taverna — calamari, grilled sardines, and bread (€8–€12)
meals.dinner: Authentic local taverna in Kalamata old town — try the local lamb kleftiko with horta (wild greens) (€10–€14)

day_by_day.notes: Kalamata is famous for its olives and olive oil — buy some at the local market as a delicious and affordable souvenir. Budget guesthouses and rooms in Kalamata average €20–€30/night.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning bus from Kalamata to Stoupa (1 hour, ~€5) — a beautiful small beach resort in the Mani region. Stoupa has two gorgeous sandy beaches side by side, crystal-clear water, and a relaxed atmosphere. Arrive early to claim a good spot.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon swimming and snorkeling at Stoupa Beach or the quieter Stoupa Kalogria Beach next door. The water clarity here is exceptional. Rent a snorkel set from a local shop (€5–€8) and explore the underwater landscape.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the small village of Stoupa on foot — it's tiny and charming. Watch the sunset from the beach with a cold Mythos beer from a local kiosk (€2–€3). Return to Kalamata by evening bus.

meals.breakfast: Greek coffee and a bougatsa (custard pastry) at a Kalamata café before departure (€2.50–€3.50)
meals.lunch: Fresh grilled fish at a simple beach taverna in Stoupa — very fresh, very local (€10–€13)
meals.dinner: Back in Kalamata — souvlaki plate with tzatziki, pita, and salad at a local grill house (€7–€10)

day_by_day.notes: Stoupa is one of the hidden gems of the Peloponnese — less touristy than the islands but with equally beautiful water. Check the bus return schedule before you go. June is ideal — warm but not yet peak-season crowded.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning ferry or bus route toward the island of Corfu (via Patras ferry port — approximately 4–5 hours total travel). Alternatively, take a direct bus to Patras (2.5 hours, ~€12) and board an afternoon ferry to Corfu (6–7 hours overnight or daytime, ~€25–€35 deck class).
day_by_day.afternoon: If taking a daytime ferry, relax on the deck, enjoy the Ionian Sea scenery, and grab affordable food from the ferry cafeteria. Arrive in Corfu Town in the late afternoon or evening.
day_by_day.evening: Check into a budget hostel or guesthouse in Corfu Town. Take a short evening walk through the beautiful UNESCO-listed Corfu Old Town — a magical labyrinth of Venetian alleyways, called 'kantounia'.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at your Kalamata guesthouse or a café near the bus station (€2–€4)
meals.lunch: Ferry cafeteria meal or packed snacks from a supermarket (€4–€7)
meals.dinner: First meal in Corfu — try 'sofrito' (veal in white wine sauce) or 'pastitsada' (spiced meat pasta) at a local taverna in the old town (€10–€14)

day_by_day.notes: This is a travel-heavy day. Book ferry tickets in advance online (Superfast Ferries or ANEK Lines) for the best budget prices. Deck/economy class is the cheapest option and perfectly comfortable in June weather. Corfu hostels average €15–€25/night.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Corfu Town's magnificent Old Town on foot — visit the Old Fortress (€6), walk through the Liston arcade, and browse the vibrant morning market near the New Port. The architecture is unlike anywhere else in Greece — a beautiful Venetian-French-British blend.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a local bus (€1.80) to Paleokastritsa on the northwest coast — arguably one of the most beautiful beach spots in all of Greece. The turquoise coves and dramatic cliffs are stunning. Swim in multiple small coves and explore the rocky coastline.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Corfu Town by bus. Walk through the Campiello district — the oldest part of the old town — as evening falls and the alleyways light up. Find a spot at a local kafeneio (traditional coffee house) and watch the world go by.

meals.breakfast: Corfu-style breakfast at a local bakery — fresh bread, local jam, and Greek coffee (€2–€3)
meals.lunch: Seafood mezedes at a small taverna at Paleokastritsa — grilled shrimp, fried calamari, and village salad (€10–€14)
meals.dinner: Budget taverna in Corfu Old Town — try 'bianco' (local white fish stew) with crusty bread and local wine (€9–€13)

day_by_day.notes: Paleokastritsa buses depart from the Corfu Town bus station (KTEL) roughly every hour. The last bus back is usually around 8–9 PM — check the schedule. Bring reef shoes as some coves are rocky.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a scooter (€15–€20/day) or bicycle (€8–€12/day) and head north along the coast to the quiet village of Kassiopi — a charming fishing village with a small beach, a Byzantine castle ruin, and an authentic local atmosphere far from the tourist crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to the nearby Canal d'Amour at Sidari — famous for its unique sandstone rock formations and sea channels carved by the waves. Swim in the natural channels and explore the beautiful coastal scenery. Entry is free.
day_by_day.evening: Return your scooter and spend the evening in Corfu Town. Visit the Municipal Gallery of Corfu (free or minimal entry) or simply wander the old town one last time as the evening lights come on.

meals.breakfast: Spanakopita (spinach pie) and coffee from a bakery near your hostel (€2.50–€3.50)
meals.lunch: Fresh catch of the day at a harbourside taverna in Kassiopi village (€9–€13)
meals.dinner: Farewell Corfu dinner — try 'kumquat liqueur' as a digestif alongside grilled lamb chops at a local grill taverna (€10–€15)

day_by_day.notes: Scooter rental requires a valid driver's license. Roads in northern Corfu are winding but manageable. Always wear a helmet. The Canal d'Amour is best visited in the morning or late afternoon to avoid midday heat.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early morning ferry back from Corfu to Patras (book in advance for best prices). Enjoy the scenic Ionian Sea crossing. Arrive in Patras mid-morning and explore this underrated Greek port city — visit the impressive Patras Castle (free entry) and the Roman Odeon.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a train or bus from Patras back to Athens (2.5–3 hours, ~€10–€14). Arrive back in Athens by mid-afternoon. Check back into your original Athens hostel or a new budget option. Do any last-minute shopping in Monastiraki for gifts and souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Athens — revisit your favorite neighborhood or explore somewhere you missed. Head to the Koukaki neighborhood near the Acropolis for a local, less-touristy Athens experience with excellent tavernas.

meals.breakfast: Quick breakfast on the ferry or from a Corfu café before departure (€2–€4)
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at Patras — try 'ladokouloura' (local sesame bread) and olives from a market (€3–€5)
meals.dinner: Final Greek dinner in Athens — splurge slightly at a Koukaki taverna, try lamb chops, grilled vegetables, and a carafe of house wine (€13–€18)

day_by_day.notes: This is another travel-heavy day. Check train and bus schedules from Patras to Athens in advance. The train (OSE) is comfortable and scenic. Use any remaining budget wisely — Monastiraki market is great for affordable local gifts like olive oil, honey, and herbs.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Athens — wake up early for one last Greek breakfast experience. Take a leisurely walk through Plaka one last time as the city wakes up. Visit any last sights you may have missed — the Roman Agora or Hadrian's Library are quick and included in the combined ticket.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Athens International Airport via the X95 express bus (€6) or Metro Line 3 (€10) with plenty of time before your departure flight. Do any last-minute duty-free shopping at the airport for Greek products like olive oil, honey, or local spirits.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Athens, carrying wonderful memories of beaches, ancient history, and incredible local food from your 13-day Greek adventure.

meals.breakfast: Classic final Greek breakfast — Greek yogurt with thyme honey, fresh fruit, and a strong Greek coffee at a Plaka café (€4–€6)
meals.lunch: Grab a final souvlaki wrap or tiropita from a street kiosk near the airport bus stop (€2.50–€4)
meals.dinner: Airport meal or on the plane

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for airport check-in and security. The X95 bus to the airport takes about 60–90 minutes from Syntagma Square depending on traffic. Keep some euros for the bus fare. Total estimated trip budget: accommodation €195–€325, transport €120–€180, food €200–€280, activities/entry fees €80–€120 — approximate total €595–€905 for 13 days.

trip_options.title: Classic Greece Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

experiences.name: Navagio Beach (Shipwreck Beach) Visit
experiences.description: Take a boat tour to the iconic Navagio Beach on Zakynthos, one of Greece's most photographed beaches. The stunning turquoise waters, towering limestone cliffs, and the famous shipwreck make this an unmissable experience. Boat tours depart regularly from Porto Vromi or Zakynthos Town.

experiences.name: Elafonissi Beach Day Trip
experiences.description: Visit the breathtaking Elafonissi Beach in southwestern Crete, famous for its pink-tinged sand and shallow crystal-clear lagoon. Wade across the sandbar to the small island, snorkel in the warm Aegean waters, and relax in one of Greece's most naturally beautiful beach settings. Accessible by bus or rental car from Chania.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled – flight arrives at 14:50
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Athens International Airport (Eleftherios Venizelos) at 14:50 via Air Serbia. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take the X95 express bus or Metro Line 3 into central Athens (approx. 40–60 min). Check in to your mid-range hotel in the Monastiraki or Koukaki neighborhood. Freshen up and take a gentle orientation stroll around Monastiraki Square and the Roman Agora to get your bearings.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the lively Monastiraki Flea Market area for a first taste of Athens. Walk up to the Acropolis base for a stunning illuminated nighttime view from Apostolou Pavlou promenade. Enjoy a relaxed first dinner in the neighborhood.

meals.breakfast: On the plane / airport snack
meals.lunch: Grab a quick gyros pita from a street kiosk near Monastiraki Square (€3–5) after settling in
meals.dinner: Dinner at Avli tou Evripidi (Monastiraki) – traditional Greek mezedes like taramosalata, grilled octopus, and spanakopita; budget €20–28 per person

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light given the afternoon arrival. Keep the evening low-key to recover from travel. Book your Athens Acropolis timed-entry ticket online tonight for Day 2 morning to avoid queues.

day_by_day.morning: Early visit to the Acropolis (open from 08:00) with your pre-booked timed ticket. Explore the Parthenon, Erechtheion, and Propylaea with stunning 360° views over Athens. Then walk down to the Acropolis Museum (open 09:00) to see the original Parthenon frieze sculptures and artifacts in a world-class modern setting.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stroll through the ancient Agora of Athens and the Temple of Hephaestus – one of Greece's best-preserved ancient temples. Walk through the charming Plaka neighborhood with its neoclassical houses and bougainvillea-draped alleys. Browse local honey, olive oil, and herb shops.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Psyrri neighborhood, Athens' bohemian quarter, for street art and vibrant café culture. Enjoy dinner with rooftop Acropolis views.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or café near Syntagma – Greek yogurt with honey and walnuts, freddo espresso (€6–9)
meals.lunch: Lunch at Cafe Avissinia in Monastiraki – hearty Greek salad, moussaka, and house wine (€15–22 per person)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Strofi Restaurant (Makrygianni) – classic Greek cuisine with Acropolis rooftop views; grilled lamb chops, horiatiki salad (€25–35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes – you'll cover 8–10 km today. The Acropolis can be very warm by midday; go early. Combined Acropolis + Ancient Agora ticket is €30, valid for 5 days across multiple sites.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the National Archaeological Museum (open 08:00), one of the world's great museums housing the Antikythera Mechanism, Mycenaean gold masks, and stunning ancient sculptures. Spend 2–3 hours exploring. Walk through the colorful Exarchia neighborhood afterward.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the Athens Riviera tram (Line T1) south to the coastal suburb of Glyfada or Vouliagmeni. Spend the afternoon at the beach – Astir Beach or Vouliagmeni Lake (a natural thermal lake with mineral-rich waters, €15 entry) are excellent mid-range options with sun loungers and clear water.
day_by_day.evening: Return to central Athens by tram/bus. Head to the upscale Kolonaki neighborhood for evening drinks at a rooftop bar, then dinner in the area.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a local bakery – bougatsa (custard-filled pastry) and Greek coffee (€4–6)
meals.lunch: Seafood lunch at a taverna near Vouliagmeni beach – grilled sea bream, tzatziki, and fresh bread (€18–25 per person)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Vezene (Kolonaki) – modern Greek cuisine; try the slow-cooked lamb and local wine selection (€28–38 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Athens Riviera gives you a first taste of Greek beach culture without leaving the capital. Vouliagmeni Lake is unique – the thermal waters are said to have therapeutic properties. Book ferry to Santorini for Day 5 tonight if not already done.

day_by_day.morning: Take a half-day trip to Cape Sounion (1.5 hrs by KTEL bus from Pedion Areos, €7 each way). Visit the stunning Temple of Poseidon perched on a cliff 60m above the Aegean Sea – one of the most dramatic ancient sites in Greece. Lord Byron carved his name into a column here.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Athens by early afternoon. Visit the vibrant Central Market (Varvakios Agora) on Athinas Street – a sensory explosion of fresh fish, meats, spices, olives, and cheeses. Pick up local snacks and provisions. Explore the nearby Omonia neighborhood.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Athens – revisit Monastiraki for souvenir shopping (local olive oil, saffron, mastiha products). Pack for early departure tomorrow. Enjoy a farewell Athens dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at hotel before departing for Sounion
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch at Cape Sounion with provisions from a local bakery or snacks bought en route (€8–12)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Diporto Agoras (hidden gem near the Central Market) – no menu, just whatever the chef cooks that day; traditional stifado, chickpea soup, barrel wine (€15–20 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Diporto Agoras is cash only and has no sign – look for the stairs going underground near Sofokleous and Theatrou streets. Cape Sounion entry is €10. Sunset at Sounion (around 20:45 in June) is spectacular but you'll need to stay later if you want it – adjust schedule accordingly.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning: Take the Blue Star Ferries or Hellenic Seaways high-speed ferry from Piraeus Port to Santorini (departs ~07:30, arrives ~12:30 high-speed, or overnight slow ferry). Check in to your mid-range hotel in Fira or Firostefani. Freshen up and have a light lunch.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Fira town – the island's capital perched on the caldera rim. Walk the caldera path from Fira toward Firostefani and Imerovigli (approx. 3 km, stunning views). Visit the Museum of Prehistoric Thera to understand the ancient Minoan civilization buried by the volcanic eruption.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the famous Santorini sunset from Imerovigli or the Skaros Rock viewpoint (less crowded than Oia). Return to Fira for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early grab-and-go breakfast at Piraeus Port – coffee and tiropita (cheese pie) (€4–6)
meals.lunch: Light lunch in Fira after arrival – mezedes platter and local Assyrtiko wine at a caldera-view café (€18–24 per person)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Mama's House Restaurant (Fira) – excellent Greek home cooking, stuffed tomatoes, fresh fish; great value (€20–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: High-speed ferry tickets: €45–65 per person one way. Book in advance for June. Santorini is expensive – mid-range here means €80–130/night for hotels. Firostefani and Karterados are more affordable than Oia while still having caldera views.

day_by_day.morning: Rent an ATV or scooter (€20–30/day) to explore the island independently. Head to the black sand beach of Perissa on the southeastern coast – dramatic volcanic black sand, clear turquoise water, and the shadow of Mesa Vouno mountain. Swim and relax.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive north along the coast to the ancient site of Akrotiri – a remarkably preserved Minoan Bronze Age city buried by volcanic ash around 1600 BCE, often called the 'Greek Pompeii' (entry €12). Then visit the red sand beach of Kokkini Paralia (Red Beach) nearby – a short hike from the parking area.
day_by_day.evening: Drive up to Oia village for the evening. Browse the iconic blue-domed churches, art galleries, and boutique shops. Stay for the sunset (arrive by 19:30 to get a good spot). Dinner in Oia.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a Fira bakery – fresh loukoumades (honey donuts) and Greek coffee (€5–8)
meals.lunch: Beachside lunch at Perissa – grilled octopus, Greek salad, and cold Mythos beer at a beach taverna (€16–22 per person)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Roka Restaurant (Oia) – local fava bean dip, grilled swordfish, Santorini cherry tomato salad (€25–35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Oia gets extremely crowded at sunset – arrive early for a good viewpoint. The path to Red Beach is rocky; wear proper shoes. Santorini's famous Assyrtiko white wine is a must-try – it's grown in volcanic soil and has a unique mineral flavor.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning caldera boat tour (€25–40 per person) from Fira's old port – visit the active volcanic islands of Nea Kameni (hike to the crater), swim in the hot springs of Palea Kameni, and stop at the picturesque village of Thirassia.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return by early afternoon. Visit the Santo Wines winery near Pyrgos village for a wine tasting session with caldera views (€18–25 for tasting flight). Explore the medieval village of Pyrgos with its Venetian castle ruins and panoramic island views.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed final evening in Santorini. Pack for tomorrow's ferry to Crete. Enjoy a farewell dinner in Fira with caldera views.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or café in Fira
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a café in Thirassia during the boat tour stop – fresh grilled fish and salad (€15–20 per person)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Naoussa Restaurant (Fira) – traditional Greek cuisine, lamb kleftiko slow-cooked in parchment, local wine (€22–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the caldera boat tour the evening before or early morning – they fill up fast in June. The volcanic hot springs are warm but not hot (around 35°C); the sulfur can stain light-colored swimwear.

day_by_day.morning: Take the morning ferry from Santorini to Heraklion, Crete (approx. 2–3 hours by high-speed, €35–50). Check in to your hotel in Heraklion or the charming old town area. Head immediately to the Palace of Knossos (4 km from city center, bus or taxi) – the legendary Minoan palace, Europe's oldest city, associated with the myth of the Minotaur and the Labyrinth.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Heraklion and visit the Heraklion Archaeological Museum – arguably the world's finest collection of Minoan art, including the famous Phaistos Disc and Minoan frescoes. Stroll along the Venetian harbor and the impressive Koules Fortress (entry €4).
day_by_day.evening: Explore the lively Lion Square (Plateia Eleftherias) and the 1866 Street market area. Enjoy dinner in the old town.

meals.breakfast: On the ferry – light snack from the ferry café
meals.lunch: Lunch near Knossos – traditional Cretan dakos (barley rusk with tomato and feta) and horta (wild greens) at a local taverna (€12–18 per person)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Peskesi Restaurant (Heraklion) – award-winning Cretan cuisine using heirloom ingredients; try the slow-roasted goat and local raki (€22–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Knossos entry is €15; combined ticket with Archaeological Museum is €20 and highly recommended. The palace reconstruction is controversial among archaeologists but visually impressive. Crete is the largest Greek island – you'll need a rental car from Day 9 to explore properly.

day_by_day.morning: Pick up a rental car in Heraklion (€30–45/day for a small car). Drive southwest (approx. 2.5 hours) to Elafonissi Beach – one of the featured experiences. This breathtaking beach in southwestern Crete is famous for its pink-tinged sand (from crushed pink shells and coral) and shallow turquoise lagoon. Arrive early to secure a good spot.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the full afternoon at Elafonissi – swim in the crystal-clear shallow waters, wade across the sandbar to the small island, snorkel in the lagoon, and relax on the unique pink-sand beach. The water is exceptionally calm and warm, perfect for swimming.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward Chania (approx. 1.5 hours from Elafonissi) and check in to a hotel there for the next two nights. Explore Chania's stunning Venetian harbor in the evening.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel in Heraklion before departing
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch at Elafonissi – bring provisions from a Chania bakery or stop at a small kiosk near the beach; fresh bread, local cheese, olives, and fruit (€8–12)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Thalassino Ageri (Chania) – exceptional fresh seafood on a terrace overlooking the sea; grilled red mullet, sea urchin salad (€25–35 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Elafonissi gets very crowded in peak June – arrive before 10:00 for the best experience. Bring your own snacks and water as beach facilities are limited. The drive through the White Mountains (Lefka Ori) is scenic – allow extra time. Sunscreen is essential on this exposed beach.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Chania's magnificent Old Town – the best-preserved Venetian harbor in Greece. Visit the covered market (Agora), the Venetian lighthouse, the Archaeological Museum of Chania (housed in a former Venetian church, entry €4), and wander the charming backstreets of the Splantzia and Topanas neighborhoods.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive east along the northern coast to Balos Lagoon (approx. 1.5 hours + 20-min walk or boat from Gramvousa Peninsula). This UNESCO-protected lagoon with turquoise and pink-hued waters is one of Crete's most beautiful spots. Alternatively, take the daily boat tour from Kissamos Port (€20 round trip) if you prefer not to drive the rough road.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Chania. Evening stroll along the Venetian harbor – one of the most romantic settings in Greece. Browse the harbor-front restaurants and shops.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a café on the Venetian harbor – Cretan graviera cheese omelet and fresh orange juice (€8–12)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch at Balos Lagoon or snacks from the boat kiosk (€8–15)
meals.dinner: Dinner at To Maridaki (Chania old town) – excellent value fresh fish taverna; fried smelt, grilled calamari, Cretan salad (€18–25 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The road to Balos is unpaved and rough – a 4WD or high-clearance vehicle is recommended, or take the boat from Kissamos instead. Balos can be windy; bring a light layer. Chania's old town is magical at night when the crowds thin out – allow time for an evening stroll.

day_by_day.morning: Drive from Chania to Zakynthos – this requires returning the Crete rental car, flying or ferrying to Zakynthos. Recommended: take an early morning flight from Chania (CHQ) to Zakynthos (ZTH) via Athens (approx. €80–130 with Aegean Airlines or Sky Express). Alternatively, take the ferry back to Piraeus and then a ferry to Zakynthos (much longer). Arrive in Zakynthos by early afternoon and check in to your hotel in Zakynthos Town or Laganas area.
day_by_day.afternoon: After settling in, head to the beautiful Gerakas Beach on the southeastern tip of the island – a protected loggerhead sea turtle (Caretta caretta) nesting beach with golden sand and clear water. Swimming is allowed but access to the nesting zone is restricted to protect the turtles.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Zakynthos Town (Chora) – the island's capital, rebuilt after the 1953 earthquake in a neoclassical Venetian style. Visit Solomos Square and the Byzantine Museum. Enjoy dinner in town.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Chania hotel before airport transfer
meals.lunch: Airport or arrival snack; light lunch near Gerakas beach – fresh salad and souvlaki at a local café (€12–16 per person)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Malanos Restaurant (Zakynthos Town) – traditional Zakynthian cuisine; try mandolato (local nougat) for dessert and local Verdea white wine (€20–28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: This is the most logistically complex day of the trip – book flights well in advance. Gerakas Beach has strict rules: no umbrellas in the nesting zone, no access after sunset. Zakynthos is famous for its sea turtles – you may spot them in the water while swimming.

day_by_day.morning: Take a boat tour to Navagio Beach (Shipwreck Beach) – one of the featured experiences and one of Greece's most iconic images. This stunning cove with a rusted shipwreck (the MV Panagiotis, stranded in 1980) surrounded by towering white limestone cliffs is only accessible by boat. Tours depart from Porto Vromi or Skinari Port (€15–25 per person). Swim in the brilliant turquoise water and explore the beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the boat tour to the Blue Caves (Kyanoun Spileon) on the northern tip of Zakynthos – sea caves where sunlight refracts through the water creating an ethereal blue glow. Snorkel in the crystal-clear water. Return to your base by mid-afternoon. Relax at a local beach (Porto Zoro or Banana Beach) in the afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks at a clifftop bar overlooking the Ionian Sea. Final island dinner in Zakynthos.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or local bakery – tiropita and Greek coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch after returning from the boat tour – fresh grilled fish at a harbor-side taverna in Skinari or Agios Nikolaos (€16–22 per person)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Arekia Restaurant (Zakynthos Town) – authentic Zakynthian recipes; stuffed rabbit, local cheese, and house wine (€22–30 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the Navagio boat tour the evening before – they sell out in peak season. The beach at Navagio has no shade and gets very hot; visit in the morning when it's cooler. The boat ride itself (30–45 min each way) can be choppy – take seasickness precautions if needed. Photography here is spectacular.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Greece – take a leisurely breakfast and a last swim at one of Zakynthos' beautiful beaches. Laganas Beach is convenient and lively, or head back to the quieter Porto Zoro for a peaceful farewell swim in the Ionian Sea. Pack and check out of your accommodation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Zakynthos Airport (ZTH) for your departure flight. If time allows before transfer, visit the Venetian Castle (Kastro) above Zakynthos Town for panoramic views over the island and the Ionian Sea – a fitting final view of Greece.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Zakynthos. If your flight connects through Athens, you may have time for a final Greek meal at the airport or in the city.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely final Greek breakfast – yogurt with local thyme honey, fresh figs, and freddo cappuccino at a beachside café (€8–12)
meals.lunch: Light farewell lunch before airport transfer – souvlaki wrap and fresh lemonade at a local grill house (€8–12 per person)
meals.dinner: Airport dining or in-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2 hours before your flight at Zakynthos Airport – it's a small airport but can get busy in peak season. Consider picking up local products as gifts: Zakynthian mandolato nougat, Cretan olive oil, Santorini wine, and Greek saffron (Kozani) are all excellent mid-range souvenirs. This concludes your 13-day balanced Greece itinerary covering Athens, Santorini, Crete, and Zakynthos.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Greece Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Navagio Beach (Shipwreck Beach) Visit
experiences.description: Take a boat tour to the iconic Navagio Beach on Zakynthos, one of Greece's most photographed beaches. The stunning turquoise waters, towering limestone cliffs, and the famous shipwreck make this an unmissable experience. Boat tours depart regularly from Porto Vromi or Zakynthos Town.

experiences.name: Athens Central Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the vibrant Varvakios Agora (Athens Central Market) and surrounding streets packed with local vendors selling fresh seafood, olives, cheeses, spices, and cured meats. Sample street food like souvlaki, spanakopita, and loukoumades from nearby stalls. A guided walking food tour enhances the experience with cultural context.

experiences.name: Elafonissi Beach Day Trip
experiences.description: Visit the breathtaking Elafonissi Beach in southwestern Crete, famous for its pink-tinged sand and shallow crystal-clear lagoon. Wade across the sandbar to the small island, snorkel in the warm Aegean waters, and relax in one of Greece's most naturally beautiful beach settings. Accessible by bus or rental car from Chania.

experiences.name: Traditional Cretan Cooking Class
experiences.description: Join a hands-on cooking class in Chania focused on authentic Cretan cuisine, one of the healthiest diets in the world. Learn to prepare dishes like dakos (barley rusk salad), lamb with stamnagathi greens, and honey-drizzled kalitsounia pastries using locally sourced ingredients. Classes typically include a market visit and a full meal.

experiences.name: Mykonos Beach Club & Local Taverna Evening
experiences.description: Spend the afternoon at Paradise Beach or Psarou Beach on Mykonos, enjoying the golden sand and clear blue waters. As the sun sets, head to a local taverna in Mykonos Town (Chora) for a traditional Greek dinner featuring fresh grilled octopus, tzatziki, fresh-caught fish, and local Assyrtiko wine at a fraction of the beach club prices.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 14:50
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Athens International Airport (Eleftherios Venizelos) at 14:50 via Air Serbia. Clear customs, collect luggage, and transfer via private luxury car service to your 5-star hotel in Athens (suggested: Hotel Grande Bretagne or Electra Metropolis). Check in, freshen up, and enjoy a welcome amenity. Take a leisurely stroll around Syntagma Square and the National Garden to ease into Greek time.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed first dinner at a refined rooftop restaurant in central Athens. Suggested: GB Roof Garden Restaurant at Hotel Grande Bretagne, offering panoramic Acropolis views, contemporary Greek cuisine, and an extensive wine list — perfect for unwinding after travel.

meals.breakfast: Enjoyed on the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: Light meal at Athens Airport arrivals hall or en route to hotel
meals.dinner: GB Roof Garden Restaurant (Hotel Grande Bretagne) — rooftop dining with Acropolis views; try the grilled sea bass with Greek herbs and a glass of Assyrtiko white wine from Santorini

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange private airport transfer before travel. Confirm hotel early check-in if possible. Keep Day 1 light — jet lag and travel fatigue are real. Pack a light jacket for the evening breeze (avg. high 23.4°C).

day_by_day.morning: Start with a lavish hotel breakfast, then embark on a guided Athens Central Market Food Tour at Varvakios Agora. Explore the vibrant market stalls overflowing with fresh fish, spices, olives, cheeses, and cured meats. A knowledgeable local guide will introduce you to vendors, explain Greek culinary traditions, and offer tastings of premium local products including aged graviera cheese, thyme honey, and loukoumades.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the market tour, visit the nearby Monastiraki Flea Market for a short browse, then head to the Acropolis Museum for an immersive deep-dive into ancient Greek history with a private guide. The museum's top-floor restaurant offers stunning views of the Acropolis itself.
day_by_day.evening: Dine at Varoulko Seaside in Mikrolimano, Piraeus — a Michelin-starred seafood restaurant by chef Lefteris Lazarou. Expect exquisitely prepared fresh seafood, creative Greek-Mediterranean dishes, and a world-class wine cellar. Reserve well in advance.

meals.breakfast: Full buffet or à la carte at your 5-star hotel
meals.lunch: Mezze-style tasting lunch included as part of the Athens Central Market Food Tour — graze on spanakopita, taramosalata, fresh bread, olives, and local cheeses at market stalls
meals.dinner: Varoulko Seaside, Piraeus — Michelin-starred; signature dishes include cuttlefish with truffle and sea urchin pasta; pair with a crisp Malagousia wine

day_by_day.notes: Book the Athens Central Market Food Tour in advance with a premium operator (e.g., Athens Insiders or Context Travel). The Acropolis Museum is closed on Mondays — confirm opening hours. Private car or taxi to Piraeus for dinner (~30 min from central Athens).

day_by_day.morning: Take an early morning private guided tour of the Acropolis and Parthenon before the crowds arrive. A licensed archaeologist guide will bring the ancient citadel to life. Afterward, wander through the charming Plaka neighborhood, the oldest district in Athens, with its neoclassical architecture, bougainvillea-draped alleys, and artisan boutiques.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the ancient Agora of Athens and the Temple of Hephaestus, then enjoy a leisurely afternoon at the Benaki Museum, which houses one of Greece's finest collections of Greek art, jewelry, and historical artifacts spanning 5,000 years.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy sundowner cocktails at a rooftop bar in Athens (suggested: A for Athens rooftop bar in Monastiraki — direct Acropolis views). Then dine at Spondi, a two-Michelin-starred restaurant in Pangrati, offering refined French-Mediterranean cuisine in a romantic garden setting.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Lunch at Strofi Restaurant near the Acropolis — traditional Greek cuisine with a rooftop terrace view of the Parthenon; try moussaka and slow-cooked lamb
meals.dinner: Spondi Restaurant, Pangrati — two Michelin stars; tasting menu with wine pairing; expect dishes like langoustine with black truffle and aged parmesan foam

day_by_day.notes: Book Acropolis tickets and guided tour online in advance to avoid queues. Spondi requires advance reservation — book at least 2 weeks ahead. Wear comfortable walking shoes for the Acropolis — the marble surfaces can be slippery.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Athens and fly to Mykonos (approx. 45-min flight; book in advance with Olympic Air or Sky Express). Check into a luxury clifftop hotel (suggested: Cavo Tagoo or Katikies Mykonos). Spend the late morning exploring the iconic Mykonos Town (Chora) — its famous whitewashed cubic architecture, blue-domed churches, and the iconic windmills at Kato Mili.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Psarou Beach or Paradise Beach for the quintessential Mykonos Beach Club experience. Rent a premium sunbed and umbrella, sip on fresh cocktails, enjoy crystal-clear Aegean waters, and soak in the vibrant atmosphere. Psarou Beach is the more exclusive option, frequented by celebrities and offering top-tier service.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Mykonos Town for the famous sunset at Little Venice — watch the sun dip into the Aegean from a waterfront bar. Then enjoy dinner at a renowned local taverna for an authentic Mykonian evening.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at Athens hotel before departure or at the airport
meals.lunch: Beach club lunch at Psarou Beach — fresh grilled octopus, Greek salad, and chilled rosé wine
meals.dinner: Nobu Matsuhisa Mykonos for a premium fusion experience, or Kiki's Tavern (no reservations — arrive early) for legendary grilled meats in a rustic garden setting

day_by_day.notes: Book Mykonos flights and accommodation well in advance — June is peak season. Psarou Beach sunbeds book up fast; reserve through your hotel concierge. Little Venice gets crowded at sunset — arrive 30 minutes early for a good spot.

day_by_day.morning: Take a private boat excursion from Mykonos to the sacred island of Delos — a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of the most important archaeological sites in Greece. Explore the ancient ruins, including the iconic Terrace of the Lions, with a private archaeologist guide. The island is uninhabited and feels like stepping back 3,000 years.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Mykonos and spend the afternoon at Ornos Beach or Agios Ioannis Beach — both more relaxed and family-friendly alternatives to Paradise Beach, with clear turquoise water and excellent beachside restaurants. Enjoy water sports or simply relax.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Mykonos Town's upscale boutiques and art galleries in the late afternoon. For dinner, head to Interni Restaurant — a chic open-air garden restaurant set in a neoclassical mansion, known for its refined Mediterranean cuisine and glamorous atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast at your Mykonos luxury property — enjoy on your private terrace or infinity pool area
meals.lunch: Beachside lunch at Scorpios Mykonos (Paraga Beach) — a bohemian beach club with outstanding Mediterranean food, fresh juices, and a beautiful setting
meals.dinner: Interni Restaurant, Mykonos Town — try the lobster pasta, grilled whole fish, and finish with loukoumades drizzled in honey and cinnamon

day_by_day.notes: Delos boats depart from the Old Port of Mykonos Town; private boat hire is recommended for a more exclusive experience. Delos is closed on Mondays — plan accordingly. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and water for the Delos visit as there is no shade on the island.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Mykonos and fly or take a high-speed ferry to Santorini (approx. 2-hour ferry or 30-min flight). Check into a luxury cave hotel in Oia or Imerovigli (suggested: Grace Hotel Santorini, Canaves Oia Suites, or Mystique). Spend the morning settling in and enjoying the jaw-dropping caldera views from your private terrace or infinity pool.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the iconic village of Oia on foot — browse the art galleries, jewelry boutiques, and artisan shops carved into the volcanic cliffs. Visit the Byzantine Castle ruins for panoramic caldera views. Take a private catamaran cruise around the caldera, stopping at the volcanic hot springs and Red and White Beaches.
day_by_day.evening: Santorini is world-famous for its sunsets — position yourself at Oia Castle or a clifftop bar (suggested: Sunset Bar at Canaves Oia) for the legendary sunset experience. Follow with a gourmet dinner at one of Oia's finest restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Brunch at a café in Mykonos Town before departure, or light snack on the ferry
meals.lunch: Upon arrival in Santorini, lunch at Ammoudi Fish Tavern in Ammoudi Bay below Oia — take the 300 steps down to the tiny port and enjoy the freshest grilled fish and seafood right by the water
meals.dinner: 1800 Restaurant in Oia — housed in a beautifully restored 19th-century captain's mansion; exceptional Mediterranean fine dining with caldera views and an award-winning wine list featuring Santorinian Assyrtiko

day_by_day.notes: Book Santorini accommodation months in advance — Oia and Imerovigli are the premium locations. The caldera catamaran cruise should be pre-booked; sunset cruises are extremely popular. Oia gets very crowded at sunset — your hotel concierge may know quieter vantage points.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the ancient Minoan city of Akrotiri — a remarkably preserved Bronze Age settlement buried by a volcanic eruption around 1627 BC, often compared to Pompeii. Hire a private guide for a deeper understanding of this extraordinary site. Afterward, visit the striking Red Beach nearby — a dramatic landscape of towering red volcanic cliffs meeting the deep blue sea.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Perissa or Perivolos Beach on the south coast — Santorini's famous black sand beaches. Relax at a premium beach club (suggested: Wet Stories or Black Sand Beach Bar). The black volcanic sand retains heat beautifully. Enjoy swimming and water sports in the clear Aegean.
day_by_day.evening: Take a private wine tour and tasting at one of Santorini's prestigious wineries — suggested: Domaine Sigalas or Santo Wines (with caldera views). Santorini's volcanic soil produces extraordinary Assyrtiko grapes. Finish the day with a candlelit dinner in Fira or Imerovigli.

meals.breakfast: In-room breakfast on your private caldera-view terrace — a quintessential Santorini luxury moment
meals.lunch: Beachside lunch at a Perissa taverna — grilled calamari, tzatziki, fresh bread, and cold Mythos beer or chilled white wine
meals.dinner: Lycabettus Restaurant, Imerovigli — stunning caldera views, sophisticated Greek-Mediterranean cuisine; try the slow-cooked lamb with herbs and the chocolate lava cake with Greek yogurt

day_by_day.notes: Akrotiri requires advance ticket purchase. Red Beach involves a short rocky walk — wear sturdy sandals. The private wine tour can be arranged through your hotel concierge. Book dinner reservations at least 2–3 days ahead in peak season.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Santorini and fly to Heraklion, Crete (approx. 1-hour flight). Check into a luxury hotel in or near Chania (suggested: Casa Delfino Boutique Hotel or Domes of Elounda). Visit the magnificent Palace of Knossos — the largest Bronze Age archaeological site in Crete and the legendary home of King Minos and the Minotaur's labyrinth.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive or transfer west to Chania — one of Greece's most beautiful cities, with its stunning Venetian harbor, lighthouse, and charming old town. Explore the narrow alleyways of the old town, the covered market, and the Venetian fortifications. Browse local shops for Cretan olive oil, herbs, and handmade leather goods.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into the magical atmosphere of Chania's Venetian harbor at golden hour. Enjoy aperitivo-style drinks at a waterfront bar, then dine at one of Chania's finest restaurants overlooking the harbor.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast in Santorini before departure
meals.lunch: Traditional Cretan lunch in Heraklion — try dakos (barley rusk with tomatoes and mizithra cheese), kalitsounia (Cretan cheese pastries), and fresh Cretan salad at a local taverna near Knossos
meals.dinner: Tamam Restaurant, Chania Old Town — set in a converted Turkish bathhouse; exceptional Cretan-Mediterranean cuisine; try the lamb with stamnagathi (wild greens) and local Cretan wine

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book a private guide for Knossos — the site is vast and complex, and a good guide transforms the experience. The drive from Heraklion to Chania takes approximately 2.5 hours — consider hiring a private driver for the day. June weather in Crete is warm and sunny — perfect beach and sightseeing conditions.

day_by_day.morning: Join a Traditional Cretan Cooking Class in Chania — a hands-on experience focused on authentic Cretan cuisine, widely regarded as one of the healthiest diets in the world. Learn to prepare dishes like dakos, stuffed vine leaves, slow-braised lamb with local herbs, and traditional Cretan pies using locally sourced ingredients. Classes typically take place in a farmhouse or olive grove setting.
day_by_day.afternoon: After your cooking class lunch, embark on the famous Samaria Gorge hike (16 km) — one of Europe's longest gorges and a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve. Alternatively, if you prefer a more relaxed afternoon, explore the Botanical Park & Gardens of Crete near Fournes, or visit the stunning Balos Lagoon by private boat from Kissamos.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Chania for a well-deserved rest and spa treatment at your hotel. For dinner, enjoy the fruits of your morning cooking class if the experience includes a take-home meal, or dine at a premium restaurant in the Venetian harbor area.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Included as part of the Cretan Cooking Class — a full traditional Cretan meal prepared by you with your instructor, paired with local Cretan wine and raki
meals.dinner: Portes Restaurant, Chania Old Town — innovative Cretan cuisine in a romantic courtyard setting; signature dishes include pork with wild mushrooms and truffle, and fresh catch of the day with capers and lemon

day_by_day.notes: Book the Cretan Cooking Class in advance through operators like Crete's Culinary Sanctuaries or Cooking Crete. The Samaria Gorge requires good physical fitness and sturdy footwear — it takes 5–7 hours to complete. The gorge is not suitable if there has been recent heavy rain. Balos Lagoon boat trip is an excellent alternative for a more relaxed afternoon.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early for the day trip to Elafonissi Beach in southwestern Crete — one of Greece's most breathtaking beaches, famous for its unique pink-tinged sand (caused by crushed coral and shells) and shallow turquoise lagoon. The drive from Chania takes approximately 1.5 hours through spectacular mountain scenery. Hire a private driver or rent a car for flexibility.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the full afternoon at Elafonissi — swim in the shallow, warm lagoon, explore the small uninhabited islet accessible by wading through ankle-deep water, and relax on the rose-tinted sand. The water is exceptionally clear and calm, making it ideal for snorkeling. Rent premium sunbeds and umbrellas for comfort.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back to Chania via the scenic coastal road, stopping at a clifftop viewpoint for photos. Return to your hotel for a shower and rest before heading out for a final Chania dinner at the Venetian harbor.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before departure to Elafonissi
meals.lunch: Beachside taverna at Elafonissi — grilled fish, Greek salad, fresh lemonade, and local Cretan white wine; the beach has a small selection of tavernas right on the sand
meals.dinner: Thalassino Ageri, Chania — legendary seafood restaurant on the waterfront; try the sea urchin pasta, grilled lobster, and fresh catch of the day; excellent Cretan wine selection

day_by_day.notes: Elafonissi is a protected natural area — no umbrellas or sunbeds are available on the main beach; bring your own or rent from nearby tavernas. Arrive early (before 10 AM) to secure a good spot, as it gets very crowded by midday in June. The road to Elafonissi is winding — allow extra time. Bring plenty of water and sunscreen.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the beautiful Chania Old Town in depth — visit the Archaeological Museum of Chania (housed in a Venetian church), the Maritime Museum of Crete at the old Venetian lighthouse, and the magnificent covered market (Agora) for last-minute Cretan food souvenirs: extra virgin olive oil, thyme honey, dried herbs, and local cheeses.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive or transfer east along the northern coast to the luxury resort area of Elounda (approx. 2 hours). Check into one of Crete's most exclusive hotels (suggested: Domes of Elounda or Blue Palace Elounda). Spend the afternoon at the hotel's private beach, infinity pool, or spa. The Gulf of Elounda is calm, warm, and strikingly beautiful.
day_by_day.evening: Take a short boat ride to the historic Spinalonga Island — a remarkably preserved Venetian fortress and former leper colony (made famous by Victoria Hislop's novel 'The Island'). Guided tours run until early evening. Return to Elounda for a premium dinner at your resort.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast in Chania
meals.lunch: Lunch en route at a traditional taverna in the village of Rethymno or Anogia — try slow-roasted lamb (antikristo) and Cretan rusks with local olive oil
meals.dinner: Blue Lagoon Restaurant at Blue Palace Elounda — fine dining with panoramic views of the Gulf of Elounda and Spinalonga; fresh seafood and contemporary Mediterranean cuisine with an exceptional Greek wine list

day_by_day.notes: Spinalonga boat trips depart from Elounda and Plaka — check last departure times. The island visit takes approximately 1.5–2 hours. Pre-book a guided tour for the best experience. The Domes of Elounda and Blue Palace are among Crete's finest resorts — book well in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a luxurious late morning at your Elounda resort — indulge in a spa treatment (suggested: a traditional Greek olive oil massage or a thalassotherapy session), swim in the private pool, or simply relax on the private beach with a good book and fresh juices. This is a well-deserved rest day after 11 days of exploration.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a private speedboat tour of the Gulf of Elounda and the surrounding coastline — explore hidden sea caves, secluded coves, and crystal-clear swimming spots inaccessible by land. Snorkeling equipment provided. Alternatively, visit the ancient Minoan site of Gournia — a remarkably preserved Bronze Age town just south of Elounda.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Crete — dress up for a truly special farewell dinner. Head to Heraklion (approx. 1 hour from Elounda) for dinner at Peskesi Restaurant — a celebrated farm-to-table restaurant dedicated to reviving ancient Cretan recipes using heritage ingredients and traditional cooking methods.

meals.breakfast: Indulgent in-room breakfast or resort terrace breakfast — fresh Cretan pastries, local honey, cheeses, yogurt with walnuts, freshly squeezed orange juice, and Greek coffee
meals.lunch: Light resort lunch at the beach club — fresh mezze, grilled calamari, watermelon, and chilled Cretan rosé
meals.dinner: Peskesi Restaurant, Heraklion — farm-to-table Cretan cuisine using heirloom recipes; try the slow-cooked goat with wild herbs, snail stew with rosemary, and the extraordinary Cretan cheese plate; pair with aged Vidiano or Kotsifali wine

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book the spa treatment at your resort. The private speedboat tour should be arranged through your hotel concierge. Book Peskesi Restaurant in advance — it is very popular and considered one of the best restaurants in Crete. Allow 1 hour transfer time to Heraklion for dinner.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Greece — enjoy a leisurely last breakfast at your Elounda resort, savoring the stunning views of the Gulf of Elounda one last time. Pack and check out, leaving luggage with the concierge. Take a final swim in the Aegean or a last stroll through the charming village of Elounda, picking up any remaining souvenirs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer to Heraklion Airport (approx. 1 hour) for your departure flight. Depending on flight time, allow time for a final coffee and pastry at a Heraklion café — try a bougatsa (warm custard-filled pastry) from the famous Kirkor or Phyllo Sofias bakeries near the Lion Fountain in Heraklion.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Heraklion International Airport (HER) for your connecting flight home via Athens or directly. Reflect on 13 extraordinary days exploring the best of Greece — from Athens' ancient wonders and Mykonos' glamour to Santorini's volcanic beauty and Crete's extraordinary culinary heritage.

meals.breakfast: Final luxurious hotel breakfast at the Elounda resort — make it count
meals.lunch: Bougatsa and Greek coffee at Kirkor bakery in Heraklion, or a light meal at Heraklion Airport
meals.dinner: Airport dining or on-board meal depending on departure time

day_by_day.notes: Confirm return flight details and check-in online 24 hours before departure. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before departure for the transfer and airport check-in. Consider purchasing premium Cretan products at the airport duty-free: olive oil, thyme honey, Cretan herbs, and local wines make excellent gifts. A private transfer from Elounda to Heraklion Airport is strongly recommended for a stress-free end to the trip.
